questions.question: [Test 34 - Q1] According to Erik Erikson's psychosocial stages of development, which conflict is primary during adolescence?
questions.explanation: Erikson identified 'Identity vs. Role Confusion' as the fifth stage of psychosocial development occurring during adolescence (ages 12 to 18). (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q2] Edward Thorndike's 'Law of Effect' states that:
options: Responses that produce a satisfying effect in a particular situation become more likely to occur again
Learning is permanent only when repeated through multiple drills
A learner must be biologically ready to acquire a new cognitive schema
Visual stimuli are remembered longer than auditory stimuli
questions.explanation: Thorndike's Law of Effect established that behaviors followed by favorable consequences are strengthened, which laid the foundation for Skinner's operant conditioning. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q3] The Maria Montessori educational method is heavily characterized by:
options: Child-centered self-directed activity, hands-on learning, and collaborative play in prepared environments
Teacher-dominated lectures and strict penal punishments
Standardized paper-and-pencil exams conducted on a weekly basis
Pre-designed digital animations with no physical tactile materials
questions.explanation: Montessori classrooms feature prepared environments, multi-sensory materials, and self-directed learning tasks where teachers guide rather than lecture. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q4] John Dewey, a pioneer of progressive education, argued that classrooms should prioritize:
options: Learning by doing and democratic cooperative inquiry
Passive listening and direct instructional lecturing
Abstract memorization of ancient classical texts
Strict separation of high IQ and low IQ students
questions.explanation: Dewey believed education is life itself, advocating experiential 'learning by doing' and training students to participate in a democratic society. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q5] In Benjamin Bloom's Mastery Learning model, what is the core assumption regarding student achievement?
options: Almost all students can master the material if provided with sufficient time and appropriate instruction
Intelligence is entirely fixed at birth and cannot be modified by pedagogical interventions
Only the top 10% of students are capable of high-order critical analysis
Written examinations should be designed to fail a high percentage of low-income pupils
questions.explanation: Mastery learning asserts that learning challenges are a function of instruction and time, rather than lack of student cognitive capacity. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q6] A student who struggles to write legibly, showing poor spatial planning on paper and difficulty with fine motor coordination, most likely suffers from:
questions.explanation: Dysgraphia is a specific learning disability that affects writing abilities, including handwriting, spelling, and organizing ideas on paper. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q7] Dyslexia is a specific learning disorder that primarily manifests as difficulty in:
options: Reading, decoding words, and phonological processing
Performing basic arithmetic and algebraic calculations
Coordinating gross motor movements in outdoor sports
Expressing verbal emotions in social gatherings
questions.explanation: Dyslexia impairs a person's ability to read and comprehend text by affecting phonological awareness, spelling, and word recognition. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q8] Which assessment type is designed to evaluate student learning, acquisition, and academic achievement at the conclusion of an instructional period?
questions.explanation: Summative assessment is 'Assessment OF Learning', occurring at the end of a unit or term (e.g., final boards, term exams) to certify achievement. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q9] In Abraham Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs, which level represents the ultimate realization of personal potential, self-fulfillment, and peak experiences?
questions.explanation: Self-actualization is the highest level of Maslow's pyramid, representing the drive to become everything that one is capable of becoming. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q10] Which educational theorist is credited with establishing 'Field Theory' in learning and pioneered Action Research in social psychology?
questions.explanation: Kurt Lewin introduced Field Theory, conceptualizing behavior as a function of the person and their psychological environment: B = f(P, E). (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q11] Jerome Bruner's concept of the 'Spiral Curriculum' advises that:
options: Complex ideas should be taught at a simplified level first, then revisited at increasing levels of difficulty
Students must study only in circular seating arrangements to improve social learning
Every topic must be completed within a single class session and never repeated
Science and mathematics must be completely separated from arts and languages
questions.explanation: A spiral curriculum revisits topics periodically with increasing depth and complexity, allowing learners to build upon their existing foundation. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q12] Noam Chomsky's theory of Language Acquisition proposes that children are born with an innate psychological mechanism known as the:
questions.explanation: Chomsky's LAD is a hypothetical biological module of the brain containing universal grammar rules that allows children to rapidly acquire any natural language. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q13] According to Robert Gagne's Conditions of Learning, how many hierarchical levels of learning are there, and what is the highest level?
questions.explanation: Gagne proposed 8 hierarchical levels of learning. The lowest is signal learning, and the highest, most complex level is problem-solving. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q14] The 'Project Method' of teaching, which focuses on solving real-world, purposeful problems in a social environment, was developed by:
questions.explanation: Kilpatrick formulated the Project Method based on pragmatism and the educational philosophies of his mentor, John Dewey. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q15] The 'Heuristic Method' of teaching, which places the student in the role of an active discoverer or researcher, was pioneered by:
questions.explanation: H. E. Armstrong developed the Heuristic Method (from the Greek 'heuriskein' meaning 'to discover') to foster scientific enquiry and self-learning. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q16] Who developed the linear model of 'Programmed Instruction', which breaks down learning material into small steps called 'frames' with immediate feedback?
questions.explanation: B. F. Skinner developed linear programmed instruction based on operant conditioning, whereas Norman Crowder developed branching programmed instruction. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q17] Which quantitative method, developed by Jacob L. Moreno, is used to measure and map social relations, attractions, and repulsions within a classroom or group?
questions.explanation: Sociometry is a tool used to visually map and analyze social structures, peer acceptance, and interpersonal relationships within a classroom. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q18] The classic formula for calculating the Intelligence Quotient (IQ), (Mental Age / Chronological Age) * 100, was first formulated by:
questions.explanation: William Stern of Germany first proposed the concept of IQ and its formula in 1912, which was subsequently adapted and popularized by Lewis Terman in the Stanford-Binet intelligence scale. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q19] According to National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, what is the new pedagogical and curricular structure replacing the existing 10+2 structure in Indian school education?
questions.explanation: NEP 2020 replaces the traditional 10+2 system with a 5+3+3+4 structure corresponding to Foundational (5 yrs), Preparatory (3 yrs), Middle (3 yrs), and Secondary (4 yrs) stages. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).

questions.question: [Test 34 - Q20] Which of the following principles best characterizes Jean Piaget's theory of cognitive development regarding the process of Schema Adaptation?
questions.explanation: Piaget defined adaptation as the balance achieved through assimilation (incorporating new info into existing schemas) and accommodation (modifying existing schemas to fit new info). (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 34).
